sentences.text: Proceratosaurus was a small carnivorous theropod dinosaur about 3 meters long from the Middle Jurassic of England.
The skull of this animal measures 26.9 cm in length.
This specific measurement applies to the only known skull of Proceratosaurus as preserved.
The lower jaw is 26 cm long, which is somewhat shorter than the skull, an unusual trait for theropods.
A narrow, elongate, kidney-shaped opening called the infratemporal fenestra is around 5.4 cm tall.
The dinosaur possessed unique D-shaped premaxillary teeth characteristic of tyrannosauroids.
A 2010 redescription estimated the holotype individual to weigh between 28 and 36 kilograms.
A 2023 study created a virtual composite model of a complete Proceratosaurus skull using data from Proceratosaurus and Guanlong skulls.
The only known specimen is a mostly complete skull with a lower jaw and hyoid bone found near Minchinhampton in Gloucestershire.
F. Lewis Bradley discovered the fossil, and Arthur Smith Woodward described it in 1910.
The type specimen was recovered in 1910 from oolitic limestone of the White Limestone Formation near Minchinhampton and is now housed in the Natural History Museum in London.
The holotype specimen has been housed at the Natural History Museum in London since 1942.
Proceratosaurus was likely a carnivore that ate relatively small prey.
Researchers suggest that Proceratosaurus likely fed on small-bodied prey based on its low bite force and skull morphology.
The cranial crest of Proceratosaurus was likely used for display.
Rauhut and colleagues suggest that the prominent head crest of Proceratosaurus was likely used as a display feature.
Proceratosaurus was originally classified as the species Megalosaurus bradleyi.
Proceratosaurus was originally classified as a species of Megalosaurus in a 1910 description by Woodward.
The genus Proceratosaurus was named by Huene in 1926.
Proceratosaurus was first described in 1910 and reclassified into its own genus in 1926.
The species name of the animal is Proceratosaurus bradleyi.
Proceratosaurus bradleyi is the only known species of the extinct genus Proceratosaurus, a ceratosaurian theropod dinosaur.
Proceratosaurus is now considered a ceratosaurian, specifically one of the earliest known members of the clade Tyrannosauroidea.
Recent studies conclude that Proceratosaurus bradleyi is a coelurosaurian tyrannosauroid belonging to the lineage leading to giant Late Cretaceous tyrannosaurs.
Proceratosaurus is classified as a coelurosaur in the family Proceratosauridae.
In the 1930s, von Huene suggested that Proceratosaurus was closely related to Ceratosaurus and considered both to be members of Coelurosauria.
Proceratosaurus is closely related to the tyrannosauroid Guanlong from the Late Jurassic of China.
Proceratosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, specifically the Bathonian age.
Proceratosaurus lived in the Middle Jurassic, approximately 167 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
Proceratosaurus lived during the Bathonian stage, from 168.2 to 165.3 million years ago.
Proceratosaurus lived in what is now England during the Middle Jurassic.
During the Middle Jurassic, Britain was located in the subtropics and formed part of an island archipelago.
Other dinosaurs known from the Bathonian age in Britain include the theropod Megalosaurus and the sauropod Cetiosaurus.
It was debated whether Piveteausaurus divesensis belonged to Proceratosaurus, but later research rejected this suggestion.
